_meta.open_decision: ASML New York registry (ASML) vs Amsterdam (ASML.AS) is NOT a liquidity question - it turns on withholding treatment and AJ Bell European dealing terms. Confirm with AJ Bell, then pin it here.

asml.pinned_reason: Raj, 05-Aug-2026: no AJ Bell platform-cost difference between the Nasdaq and Amsterdam lines, so the decision falls to the remaining differences. (1) WITHHOLDING IS THE SAME: ASML is Dutch-domiciled, so BOTH lines pay a Dutch dividend and suffer 15% Dutch withholding; the New York registry shares are NOT an ADR wrapper and W-8BEN does not apply, so there is nothing to reclaim on either line inside an ISA. Withholding therefore does not discriminate. (2) LIQUIDITY AND SPREAD: Amsterdam is the PRIMARY listing and carries the deeper book, so the dealing spread is tighter — the same reason the listing policy prefers the more liquid line everywhere else. (3) FX: both are non-GBP and both attract the 0.50% charge, so FX does not discriminate either. Amsterdam wins on the only axis that differs. REVERSIBLE: change `ticker` here and state why.
asml.confirm_with_broker: Not a blocker, but worth confirming once with AJ Bell: European dealing is available on the account and the EUR line settles normally. If Amsterdam turns out to be unavailable or more expensive to deal, flip this to ASML and record that as the reason.
